author: Georgos
text_post: Hi, I'm new to the forum, don't know if this kind of group therapy will be helpful but I am hopeful  Basically I was a virgin until I was 33, when I had sex twice with a hypersexual girl I met at some group therapy sessions for people with mental health problems, which I have. I have never had sex since, I'm now 37. I don't want to go over analysing the relationship I had, which lasted six months, but I will say that I am unlikely to find another person with an attitude towards both me and sex that is the same. It was a definite one off and I'm not sure very healthy for either of us. However it did put things in perspective, lifting a great weight off my shoulders. Before that I had worked up the courage to join a dating website. I have been on that website for about seven or eight years and been on a reasonable number of dates since I began. None of them have had any remotely sexual interaction. The difficulty I have is in sharing sexual desires. I fail to respond when there are sexual cues, doubting myself and the other, and I am unable to initiate sexual cues myself due to fear. I can quite happily have an asexual conversation, but this is not the point of the exercise. Are there any success stories by others on this forum of guys who have successfully overcome these problems? I would love to know. Thank you.

author: ukshygirl
text_post: Welcome to the forum  Hope you don't mind a response from a woman but since none of the guys stepped in to connect with you yet, I thought I would say hello as I didn't want you to feel like you're talking to yourself. I hear you on struggles, even though it's coming from a different standpoint. I am hopeless at initiating sexual cues as well within dating and in a way, I feel like it is the woman's job to do so as sometimes it can come off badly when men initiate too direct sexual cues. On dating sites, we would get messages from guys who are all about sex right away in their discussions and first message. This is off putting and I found often the best people who were decent and wanted to be more subtle actually come off so much better and shouldn't worry over showing some sexual interest in light flirting.

author: oncebitten55
text_post: Loveshy.com is not the same as group therapy, Georgos. This particular sub-section, the Lighthouse, is for love-shy's only, of course. That said, I am very glad that you did get laid by this "hyper-sexual" woman, but to be frank, you simply got lucky, not that it was a bad thing at all.  I "got lucky" at an earlier age, but after that it was "game-on". Women/pussy can be as addictive as a narcotic drug. I must add at this point that I am a former love-shy man, who didn't get laid until my latter 20's, and I have gone over to the MGTOW camp, only using women as cum-dumpsters, and that isn't very often, by my own choice, these days. No, I dont hate women at all, but I now understand them and I only wish I could go back in time to educate my younger self. You may well not be ready for the "Red-Pill" at 37 (I wasn't, as I was still chasing "pussy" at that age), but there may come a time when you will need to understand WHY women act as they do. It's really pretty simple, once you read about all of it. I would like to ask you a question, that does happen to many love-shy men: Have you ever had a "oneitis"? My guess is that you have, and likely more the one as well, at your age. FYI, a "oneitis" is a girl/woman that you, for whatever reason, cannot get off your mind. You may even feel that you "love" her, even if you have never properly even met her. You may not be able to wish to be with any other women at all, but her. This condition seems to be even more of a hallmark/ very _bad_ experience, and very prevalent amongst love-shy men.

author: OdDCy
text_post: I'm still struggling to overcome my problems, although I've had great success in the past.  The best, and most awkward thing you can do is break the touch barrier.  You have to make a comment and then punctuate it by touching her on the shoulder for no reason at all.  Because of our natural shame when it comes to shows of "sexual behavior" it feels awkward, creepy, and slimy when you do it, but you must do it.  If she likes you  she won't mind it, and if she doesn't, then she'll begin giving you the "I'm not into you" vibe that she would have given to you later anyway.  Once you break the touch barrier, she'll feel comfortable later to touch you back.   That's the first step.  I'm too depressed to talk about the other steps with clarity right now.
